title: The Truth About Extended Warranties at Dealerships
summary: A dealer-finance employee calls dealership extended warranties overpriced service contracts and describes starting an in-house warranty after seeing claims denied.

assertions.quote: if you're buying a used car at a dealership and they're trying to sell you an extended warranty, it's technically a service contract
They likely pay, let's say it's $500, they're going to charge you two grand for it.
they make you make the decision right there on the spot and I don't think that's fair

verdicts.note: High-pressure, same-visit add-on sales in the finance office are a widely reported dealership practice.

FTC says dealers "typically mention auto service contracts... after you've spent a long day at the dealership" or slip them into paperwork "without discussing them with you," consistent with limited time to consider, though not framed as explicit pressure to decide immediately.

assertions.quote: typically they would deny the claim and then we'd end up paying it anyway
